title: SDK Hot-Reload & Contract Test Harness Playbook
author: Priya Narang
content:
Overview:

This playbook describes the recommended developer experience for iterating on Redwood SDKs with fast local hot-reload, a deterministic contract test harness, and CI-integrated snippet validation. It is intended for SDK owners, DX engineers, and on-call support engineers. The goal is to reduce developer iteration time while preventing regressions at merge-time and in production.

Sections in this page:
- Purpose and scope
- System components and who owns them
- Local quickstart: hot-reload + contract test runner
- CI integration: gates, snippet validation, and flaky mitigation
- Canonical support fixes and triage checklist
- Observability and quality metrics
- Rollout notes and ownership
- Appendix: example configs and commands

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Make it fast and safe to change SDK code paths that affect request/response semantics, streaming/handshake behavior, and telemetry.
- Scope: All official Redwood client SDKs (JS, Python, Go, and the reference CLI). This playbook focuses on the parts of SDKs that interact with the inference API surface (generation/chat/embeddings/streams) and the CI hooks that validate consumption contracts.

System components (high level):
- dx-local-proxy (owned by eng-devx): a lightweight local proxy that mirrors API surface and supports deterministic fixtures and replay.
- sdk-contract-runner (owned by eng-devx): a command-line harness that runs JSON-schema based contract checks and golden-response assertions.
- snippet-validator (owned by docs-team + eng-devx): executes documentation snippets against a pinned runtime to prevent drift.
- sdk-ci (owned by eng-platform): CI workflows that run linters, unit tests, contract-runner, and snippet-validator before merges.

Quickstart: Hot-reload + contract test runner (local)
1) Prereqs:
   - Node 18+ (for JS SDK), Python 3.10+ (for Python SDK), Go 1.20+ (for go-sdk), Docker (for local proxy).
   - RBAC: developer account with API key via Console > API Keys > "dev-local" (scoped to dev sandbox).

2) Start the local proxy (replays and fixtures):
   - Command: docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/redwood-inference/dx-local-proxy:stable 
   - The proxy provides two modes: --replay (serves saved fixtures) and --record (captures live interactions).

3) Hot-reload loop for the SDK(s):
   - Recommended dev flow (JS example):
     1. Start TypeScript watch with: npm run dev:watch (invokes tsc -w + rollup dev).
     2. Start local test runner: ./scripts/contract-watch.sh 
     3. contract-watch.sh uses chokidar to watch src/ and triggers the sdk-contract-runner on change.

4) Run the contract harness manually:
   - Example (JS): ./bin/sdk-contract-runner --sdk js --fixtures ./contracts/golden-responses --schema ./contracts/response-schema.json
   - The runner validates: JSON schema conformance, required headers, streaming chunk sequence, and canonical tokenization (if applicable).

5) Interpreting results:
   - green = all contracts pass.
   - amber = schema warnings (non-blocking in local dev).
   - red = failing contract assertions (must be fixed before merge).

Contract test design notes:
- Keep golden response fixtures intentionally small and focused on surface semantics, not model text. Use placeholders: {{SENTENCE}} and validate token alignment only where behavior is contract-critical.
- Validate streaming handshakes by asserting order of first N control frames: [OPEN, META, CHUNK_START].
- Schema files live in /contracts/*.json and follow the Draft-07/2020 specification.

CI integration: gates and policies
- CI pipeline stages (order matters):
  1. lint
  2. unit tests
  3. sdk-contract-runner (fast-mode)
  4. snippet-validator (docs snippets)
  5. integration tests (flavor: against staging or recorded fixtures)

- Time budget: keep the contract-runner fast-mode under 90s. If full contract-suite exceeds 10min, run a representative subset in the PR gate and schedule full run in nightly builds.

- GitHub Actions snippet (canonical):
```yaml
name: SDK PR checks
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - name: Install
        run: npm ci
      - name: Lint and unit tests
        run: npm run lint && npm test --silent
      - name: Contract fast-mode
        run: ./bin/sdk-contract-runner --fast
      - name: Snippet validator
        run: ./bin/snippet-validator --fail-on-diff
```

- Flaky mitigation: mark tests as flaky in the registry with /flaky tag and apply auto-retry (max 2) only for flaky-marked jobs. Collect flakiness metrics in Datadog.

Snippet validation and docs site integration:
- snippet-validator runs each code block in markdown files against the dx-local-proxy using pinned fixture sets. It records stdout/stderr and diffs against golden outputs.
- PR blocking mode uses --fail-on-diff. A non-blocking mode (docs-only changes) can run with --report-only to create a docs-ticket if diffs appear.

Canonical support fixes and triage checklist (top issues):
- Symptom: "Streaming handshake fails intermittently"
  - Quick checks:
    1. Reproduce locally: run dx-local-proxy --replay streaming-handshake-failure.json and run the SDK demo stream example.
    2. Check SDK logs: look for mismatched frame IDs or missing "meta" frame (log key: sdk.stream.handshake).
    3. If reproducible, run sdk-contract-runner with --trace to capture packet-level ordering.
  - Fix pattern: ensure the client sends OPEN then META before any CHUNK. Add an idempotent retry for handshake that uses exponential backoff with jitter.

- Symptom: "Tokenization mismatch in golden tests after model update"
  - Quick checks:
    1. Confirm which model variant the fixture used (metadata in fixture header).
    2. If the model changes are expected, update the fixture using ./bin/fixture-refresh --model=model-x --approve (requires reviewer approval).
  - Fix pattern: pin tokenization checks to token-profile tolerant mode (allow small token deltas) and add regression alerting.

- Symptom: "Snippet output drift (docs)"
  - Quick checks:
    1. Run ./bin/snippet-validator --file path/to/doc.md --record to re-run and inspect golden diffs.
    2. If the change is intended, update golden via PR and include a short reason in the commit message: docs: update snippet for api-change <PR-ID>.

Observability and quality metrics:
- Victory metrics to track in Datadog/SLO dashboards:
  - PR gate pass rate for contract-runner (target 98% on first try).
  - Average local feedback loop time (save->contract-runner finish) (target < 8s for unit-level runs, < 90s for full fast-mode).
  - Snippet diffs per month (trend down).
  - Flakiness index: percent of runs requiring >1 retry. Target < 1.5%.

- Instrumentation suggestions:
  - sdk-contract-runner emits structured telemetry: event=contract_run, sdk=js, duration_ms, result={pass|warn|fail}, fixture_id.
  - snippet-validator emits: snippet.hash, file.path, diff.size, run.mode.

Rollout notes and ownership:
- Owners:
  - eng-devx: feature owner for dx-local-proxy and sdk-contract-runner.
  - docs-team: owner for snippet-validator integration.
  - eng-platform: owner for CI workflows and runners.

- Rollout strategy for new contract assertions:
  1. Add assertion behind feature flag in contract-runner (non-blocking) and monitor failures for 2 weeks.
  2. Promote to fast-mode blocking once the signal is stable (failures < 0.5% of PRs).

Appendix: example configs and helper scripts
- Example contract-runner config (YAML):
```yaml
sdk: js
mode: fast
fixtures_dir: ./contracts/golden-responses
schema: ./contracts/response-schema.json
timeout_ms: 60000
telemetry: true
```

- Example local watch script (scripts/contract-watch.sh):
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# lightweight watch loop used by DX contributors
while inotifywait -e modify -r src/ contracts/; do
  ./bin/sdk-contract-runner --fast --report || echo "contract check failed (local)"
done
```

- Troubleshooting commands (quick):
  - Start proxy in record mode: docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/redwood-inference/dx-local-proxy:stable --record
  - Run single fixture: ./bin/sdk-contract-runner --sdk js --fixture-id streaming-handshake-01 --trace
  - Validate snippets for a single file: ./bin/snippet-validator --file docs/examples/streaming.md --fail-on-diff

Contact and escalation:
- Primary contact: eng-devx@redwood.com (pager: #eng-devx on Slack).
- On-call triage: follow the oncall playbooks in /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues (link in related pages).
